excerpt: Vendease is a Nigerian B2B food procurement platform for restaurants and hotels, now offering Lagos kitchens buy-now-pay-later stock, 7-day price locks and one consolidated invoice. Backed by Y Combinator, TLcom and Partech.
content:
Vendease is a Nigerian startup that helps restaurants, hotels and other food businesses buy their supplies. Instead of dealing with several market traders and wholesalers, a kitchen orders proteins, seafood, produce, staples, oils and packaging from Vendease and gets one delivery and one invoice. Its website today focuses on Lagos: it delivers across Lekki, Victoria Island, Ikoyi, Ikate and other zones, holds each price for seven days, and offers buy-now-pay-later credit to verified operators, with a stated daily rate of 0.2% and up to ₦6 million of credit per account. Orders can be placed on the website or on WhatsApp.

TechCrunch reported in March 2021 that Vendease was founded by Tunde Kara, Olumide Fayankin, Gatumi Aliyu and Wale Oyepeju, friends who noticed favourite restaurants in Lagos and Accra closing and heard that unreliable, expensive food procurement was a big reason. The company was backed by Y Combinator. Before Vendease the founders had built an adtech startup for ride-hailing companies that did not last.

In September 2022 TechCabal reported that Vendease raised $30 million in equity and debt: a $20 million Series A co-led by TLcom Capital and Partech, plus $10 million of debt. At the time it said it was present in eight cities across Nigeria and Ghana, made bulk-buy deals with suppliers, warehoused food and guaranteed next-day delivery, and had moved more than 400,000 tonnes of food through its platform in the previous twelve months. TLcom's Andreata Muforo and Partech's Cyril Collon joined its board.

The current website describes a narrower, Lagos-focused service than the 2022 coverage; we have not found a public statement explaining the change. This profile draws on Vendease's own site and published reporting. We have not used the service, and nothing here is paid placement.

pricing.intro: Vendease publishes live per-item prices in its online catalogue (for example, per-kilogram prices for chicken), held for seven days. Its buy-now-pay-later credit for verified operators carries a stated rate of 0.2% a day, with up to ₦6 million of credit per account and approval in about 48 hours.
